مَرْهُوبٌ Feared: (Mgh, Msb:) [or feared with caution:] applied to God. (Msb.) In the phrase لَبَّيْكَ مَرْهُوبٌ وَمَرْغُوبٌ إِلَيْكَ [At thy service time after time: Thou art feared, and petitioned, or supplicated with humility, &c.], it is in the nom. case as the enunciative of an inchoative [أَنْتَ] suppressed. (Mgh.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] المَرْهُوبُ, as also ↓ الرَّاهِبُ , [the latter in this case being like رَاضٍ in the sense of مَرْضِىٌّ,] The lion. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
